title: Moments of a centered two-point law
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $0\le\lambda\le1$. Suppose $\mu(X=1-\lambda)=\lambda$ and $\mu(X=-\lambda)=1-\lambda$. Then $\int X\,d\mu=0$, and the square of the real-valued random-variable norm at exponent $2$ is $N_2(X)^2=\lambda(1-\lambda)$.
replaced: Let $X$ be measurable on a probability space and let $0\le\lambda\le1$. If $\Pr[X=1-\lambda]=\lambda$ and $\Pr[X=-\lambda]=1-\lambda$, then $\E X=0$ and $\|X\|_2^2=\lambda(1-\lambda)$.
